title: Conformal soft modes at elastic instabilities
authors: Lars Franke, Nick Sander, Markus Garst
abstract: In case a crystal is close to a continuous elastic phase transition, pronounced critical fluctuations emerge. We show that on the level of linear elasticity theory the displacement vector for these critical modes obeys a condition reminiscent of the conformal Killing equation. For an isostructural instability, four critical modes arise corresponding to one dilation and three special conformal transformations. At crystal symmetry-breaking instabilities, the critical fluctuations include a continuum of modes even for crystals with finite size. For certain cases, these comprise the conformal transformations associated with two-dimensional Minkowski space. These results have implications for critical elastic phenomena as well as for extremal mechanical metamaterials.
summary: This work investigates the mathematical nature of critical fluctuations in crystals approaching elastic phase transitions. It shows that the associated zero modes satisfy equations related to the conformal Killing equation. The findings provide a systematic classification of these critical modes, which have implications for understanding mechanical metamaterials and critical elastic behavior.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the critical fluctuations and zero modes of the displacement field in crystalline solids near continuous elastic phase transitions (elastic instabilities).
main_result: The critical modes obey a condition reminiscent of the conformal Killing equation, yielding specific sets of zero modes (e.g., dilation and three special conformal transformations for isostructural instability).
method: The analysis uses linear elasticity theory, deriving zero mode conditions from the vanishing internal stress ($\partial_i u_j + \partial_j u_i = \sum \lambda_\alpha \varepsilon^A_{ij}$) and comparing these solutions to known mathematical structures.
model_or_system: The system is crystalline solids undergoing elastic instabilities, modeled using the displacement vector $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x})$ and the strain tensor $\varepsilon_{ij}$. The analysis is generalized to extremal mechanical metamaterials.
key_observables: Critical modes of the displacement field, principal strains ($\epsilon_\alpha$), and the vanishing of the determinant of principal strains.
important_parameters: Elastic eigenmoduli ($C_\alpha$), the dimensionality of the critical subspace ($\Gamma$), and the wavevector $\mathbf{q}$ in Fourier space.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to linear elasticity theory and assumes the absence of external stresses; later notes suggest the initial assumption of analyticity for $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{q})$ is too restrictive.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the macroscopic zero modes for both volumetric singlet (dilation and SCT) and symmetry-breaking instabilities, showing the functional form of the displacement field.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the zero mode condition by first establishing the connection to the conformal Killing equation for isostructural instabilities, then extending the analysis to symmetry-breaking instabilities, and finally using group theory and determinant analysis to constrain the principal strains.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state elasticity, the mathematical framework—relating critical fluctuations to conformal symmetries—is highly relevant to theoretical physics dealing with scale invariance, critical phenomena, and emergent symmetries in many-body systems.
